text: Why is private college tuition forty-five K here… and zero at most German public schools?
That's the average private college in America. Forty-five thousand. Just tuition.
Four years? One hundred eighty thousand dollars. Before rent. Before food.
In Germany, public universities charge no tuition. Not for Germans. Not for Americans. Yes — you can go.
You pay a semester fee. A few hundred euros. Usually with a bus pass.
So why isn't every American going?
Catch one: most bachelor's programs are taught in German.
Catch two: a U.S. high school diploma often isn't enough. They usually want A.P. scores, or a year of college.
Catch three: for the visa, you need about twelve thousand euros in a blocked bank account.
That's your living money. About a thousand euros a month.
But the tuition math is brutal. One hundred eighty thousand dollars… versus zero.
Meanwhile, the average American borrower owes about thirty-nine thousand five hundred dollars in federal student loans.
Germany isn't free money. But it's a one-hundred-eighty-thousand-dollar tuition difference.
Would you move to Germany for a free degree? Comment below.
